endpoints.name: Blocked Items
endpoints.description: Everything excluded from tracking -- bots, IP addresses and visitors. WORTH READING BEFORE TRUSTING TRAFFIC FIGURES: an exclusion rule changes every number in the trends tables and appears nowhere in them.

endpoints.name: Blocked Bots
endpoints.description: The bot exclusions in force.

endpoints.name: Blocked IPs
endpoints.description: The IP addresses excluded, which is typically how a company filters its own staff out of its analytics.

endpoints.name: Blocked Visitors
endpoints.description: The individual visitors excluded.

endpoints.name: Feeds
endpoints.description: The activity feeds available on the account.

endpoints.name: Report Preferences
endpoints.description: The report and notification preferences configured. Configuration.

endpoints.name: Team Members
endpoints.description: The users with access to the account.

endpoints.name: Sites
endpoints.description: The sites tracked on the account, with their tokens. EVERY OTHER ENDPOINT NEEDS A SITE TOKEN, so this is the first request. The presenter parameter changes the response shape -- grouped or flat -- which is a pattern throughout this connector and worth noticing, since the same endpoint returns structurally different JSON depending on it.

endpoints.name: Site Domains
endpoints.description: The domains registered for one site. Requires a site token. Traffic is only tracked from these, so an unexpected gap in data often traces back to a domain that was never registered.

endpoints.name: Site Domain
endpoints.description: One domain by name. Requires the site token.

endpoints.name: Tagged Visitors
endpoints.description: The visitors carrying tags. Tags are the manual segmentation of individuals, as opposed to the rule-based smart groups.

endpoints.name: Trigger Types
endpoints.description: The trigger types webhooks can subscribe to. Reference data.

endpoints.name: Webhooks
endpoints.description: The webhooks configured. Integration configuration.

endpoints.name: Webhook
endpoints.description: One webhook by id.

endpoints.name: Webhook Triggers
endpoints.description: The triggers attached to one webhook. Requires a webhook id.

endpoints.name: Online Browsers
endpoints.description: The browsers current visitors are using.

endpoints.name: Online Campaigns
endpoints.description: The marketing campaigns current visitors arrived through.

endpoints.name: Online Concurrent Visitors
endpoints.description: How many people are on the site right now.

endpoints.name: Online Countries
endpoints.description: Where current visitors are, by country.

endpoints.name: Realtime Engagement
endpoints.description: The live engagement measure -- how actively current visitors are interacting rather than merely present.

endpoints.name: Online Geographic User Info
endpoints.description: Current visitors by geography in more detail, filterable by visitor mode.

endpoints.name: Online Languages
endpoints.description: The browser languages of current visitors.

endpoints.name: Online Notifications
endpoints.description: The notifications raised for the site over a period -- traffic spikes, goals met, alerts fired. The events GoSquared thought worth flagging.

endpoints.name: Online Organizations
endpoints.description: The organisations current visitors resolve to, from their IP addresses. B2B attribution -- which companies are on the site now, which no consumer analytics tool offers.

endpoints.name: Realtime Overview
endpoints.description: The live headline figures for a site -- concurrent visitors, pages viewed, and the current engagement summary. THE NOW API IS A SNAPSHOT: everything under it describes this instant and keeps no history, so a trend can only be built by sampling repeatedly. The trends endpoints below are the historical ones.

endpoints.name: Online Pages
endpoints.description: The pages being viewed right now, with their visitor counts.

endpoints.name: Online Platforms
endpoints.description: The operating systems and devices of current visitors.

endpoints.name: Online Sources
endpoints.description: Where current visitors came from, by section -- direct, search, social, referral.

endpoints.name: Current Time
endpoints.description: GoSquared's own clock. Useful for anchoring a relative range to the service's time rather than the caller's.

endpoints.name: Time Series
endpoints.description: A live time series over a short recent window. The bridge between the instantaneous now API and the historical trends API.

endpoints.name: Visitors
endpoints.description: The individual visitors currently on the site, filterable to all, tagged or returning. The person-level live view, as opposed to the counts.

endpoints.name: Historical Aggregate Data
endpoints.description: Site totals over a date range -- visits, page views, unique visitors and engagement. THE TRENDS API IS THE HISTORICAL ONE, in contrast to the now API above, and this is its headline table.

endpoints.name: Historical Browser Data
endpoints.description: Traffic by browser over a date range.

endpoints.name: Historical Campaign Content
endpoints.description: Traffic by campaign content -- utm_content, which distinguishes creative variants.

endpoints.name: Historical Campaign Medium
endpoints.description: Traffic by campaign medium -- utm_medium.

endpoints.name: Historical Campaign Name
endpoints.description: Traffic by campaign name over a range -- the utm_campaign dimension.

endpoints.name: Historical Campaign Source
endpoints.description: Traffic by campaign source -- utm_source.

endpoints.name: Historical Campaign Term
endpoints.description: Traffic by campaign term -- utm_term, the paid keyword.

endpoints.name: Historical Country Data
endpoints.description: Traffic by country over a date range.

endpoints.name: Historical Event Data
endpoints.description: Custom events recorded over a date range. Events are whatever the site's own code sends, so their names and meanings are entirely account-specific.

endpoints.name: Historical Language Data
endpoints.description: Traffic by browser language over a date range.

endpoints.name: Historical Organization Data
endpoints.description: Traffic by resolved organisation over a date range. The historical B2B view, and the basis for account-based marketing questions.

endpoints.name: Historical OS Data
endpoints.description: Traffic by operating system over a date range.

endpoints.name: Historical Page Data
endpoints.description: Page views over a date range, by page. Which content earned the traffic.

endpoints.name: Historical Base Path Data
endpoints.description: Traffic grouped by the FIRST path segment over a range. The section-level view -- blog, product, docs -- which the per-page table cannot give without manual grouping.

endpoints.name: Historical Screen Dimensions Data
endpoints.description: Traffic by screen size over a date range. What a responsive design actually has to serve.

endpoints.name: Historical Sources Data
endpoints.description: Traffic by referral source over a date range. The acquisition table.

endpoints.name: People CRM Devices
endpoints.description: The devices seen, each linked to the person using it. One person can have several, which is why device counts and people counts differ.

endpoints.name: People CRM Device
endpoints.description: One device by id.

endpoints.name: People CRM Event Types
endpoints.description: The event types recorded against people. The vocabulary of behaviours being tracked.

endpoints.name: People CRM Search
endpoints.description: People in the GoSquared CRM matching a query. THIS IS THE IDENTITY LAYER: analytics elsewhere counts anonymous sessions, and People links those sessions to named individuals with properties and event history -- so it is what turns traffic into accounts.

endpoints.name: People CRM Person
endpoints.description: One person by id, with their properties and activity.

endpoints.name: People CRM Property Types
endpoints.description: The properties people can carry, standard and custom. The decoder for the property keys on a person.

endpoints.name: People CRM Custom Property Types
endpoints.description: Only the custom properties defined. What the business chose to record about people, which is entirely account-specific.

endpoints.name: People CRM Property Type
endpoints.description: One property type by id.

endpoints.name: People CRM Smart Groups
endpoints.description: The smart groups defined -- audiences described by rules over properties and behaviour rather than by explicit membership. Their rules state the business's own segment definitions.

endpoints.name: People CRM Smart Group
endpoints.description: One smart group by id, with its rules and current membership count.

endpoints.name: Archived Chats
endpoints.description: Closed chat conversations over a period. The historical record; active chats move here when they end.

endpoints.name: Active Chats
endpoints.description: Live chat conversations over a period. The support channel alongside the analytics.

endpoints.name: Active Chat
endpoints.description: One chat by id, with its messages.
